utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, this is Case IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness Y.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: We shall resume the cross-examination that we started yesterday, and let me remind you that we were talking about events at Rondo yesterday during your testimony. You said that soldier nicknamed Tsotsa was beaten once again. My question is: Did you watch personally as these soldiers beat Tsotsa at Rondo? Did you see that personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far were you and what was your position in relation to that event? Could you see it well or --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was 2 or 3 metres ahead of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Tell us, was Tsotsa taken back to the Heliodrom with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yesterday, you repeatedly mentioned the name of Hasib Lulic, one of the prisoners who was with you. Was he present at the event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Is Hasib Lulic the person who told you who Stela was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did he tell you that on site at that same place or did he tell you that later at Heliodrom or wherever?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: He first addressed Stela down there when Stela asked him, What are you doing here? And he said, well, you know, Stela was in Capljina, and I came to see my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: When did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that at Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: That Hasib Lulic, does he know you personally? When we confront him with your testimony, will he remember you, your name, and that incident? Can he confirm all this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And tell me, please, have you been following this case of late in the media, or rather, did you have an opportunity to see Stela's photograph on television or in the papers? Have you been following this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the case, and I do from time to time follow the trial but I did not see Stela.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I do not know whether it would be better if I did re-cross first, because we have received the signed statements. It is up to you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, up to now, we have not received it yet. Yes, Mr. Stringer. You want to explain this matter to us?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. This is a statement. The statement at issue yesterday was dated, I believe, the 9th of December, '98, and it has been now forwarded to the Bench in all three languages in which it exists, French being the original language version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, yesterday during your cross-examination, we have already promised you that when we got those documents, you have the opportunity to cross-examine this witness. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness Y.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let me remind you, yesterday we talked about your statement that you gave on the 9th of December, '98. You said that you never uttered this particular sentence. I can put it before you, if you want me to, but I suppose you read it yesterday. But let me remind you. It reads as follows: I need to add that through the window of my cell at the Heliodrom, I saw Tuta twice visiting the camp. On both occasions, he would come in a white Audi, accompanied by a soldier. On the first occasion, he was accompanied by Juka. On the other occasion, he was alone. He never visited prisoners. He would stay in the vicinity of administrative buildings. We have received your original statement, and there is your signature here that says that you have read this statement and confirmed it with your signature. Now, will you please tell me, did you speak the truth then, and is that statement in its entirety true, or perhaps isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true that I ever said anything like this. I could not say that I saw him through the window twice. On the first occasion, I saw him through the window but I was on the upper floor, and the second time I was in the prison. I only saw him arrive in Audi 100 on the first occasion when Juka was there, and I never stated what you just read to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You want to say that this is untrue what it says in your statement. Then how could it then happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know how it could happen, but I never said anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, will you please be so kind and tell me if you read the statement in your language prior to signing it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot exactly remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think in response to the last question, at this point it might be the most fair to allow the witness to look at the document which bears his signature, if he is being asked whether he signed it or not. That's my suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That is a legitimate request. Maybe usher could show the witness the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours. I thought that the witness had the French version.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that there is my signature in one place. This is my signature. But how that text was changed, I really have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But each one of the pages is signed, and it also says that you read it and confirmed the veracity. So every page is signed, and there is also a signature at the end.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember when I gave all those statements in Sarajevo. One of the statements that I signed, they read it out to me and asked me to sign it, and that is what I did. And when they read it out to me, I thought that it was just as I had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My last question: Is it your signature on every page, including under the sentence which says that you read the statement and confirm it? Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: My signature is on each one of these pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That will be all, Your Honours. I do not have any further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. At this time I would ask the witness be given a copy of his -- a different statement made by him in April of 1997. For the record, I am handing the witness the original English version bearing his signature as well as the B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness Y, can you just take a moment to look at those two documents. Let me ask you first this: If you would look at the English version, if you could look at the front page of that and the other pages and tell me whether the English version of your document bears your signature.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And now, the other document that's in front of you, does that appear to be a translation of your statement into your own language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom of the front page of that statement, it indicates the date of the interview. Do you see that? I'm sorry, on the last page. The last page with the certification, there are dates appearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What are the dates that you see there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: 29th of April, '97.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, I would like to direct your attention to page 7 of the Bosnian version of that statement, and I want to ask you if you see words relating to the second visit or a second visit by Tuta, I believe beginning on the fourth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a correct statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Beginning with the words, "The second time I saw him..." could you just read what your statement says.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The second time I saw him, while I was in a cell, Tuta was touring the cells, including the cell that I was in. The police officers who were with Tuta opened the door and asked me to introduce myself to Tuta. Tuta then said that the conditions in the cell were better than I deserved. This is what happened while Tuta was there."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, now, Witness, your statement then continues with a description of Tuta and I would like you to skip that, and then move down to the second paragraph after that, which begins with the words "Twenty minutes later..."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Twenty minutes later, five more military policemen came, took me out of the cell into the passage, and started to beat me. They beat me with a shovel handle and rubber police batons. They struck me several times, and I began to bleed. I was ordered -- they ordered me to lick the floor because they should not have any balija blood on the floor. Then they struck me with something hard on the head and I fainted. Since then, I have a hole in my head so big that I can put two fingers in it. This statement -- I made this statement to the best of my recollection. If necessary, I am ready to provide further information to the International Tribunal."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now you can set those statements aside. Now, what you've just read, is that your testimony about one of the occasions when you saw Tuta in the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to go back and ask you just a few questions about the events in Sovici in April of 1993. On the day of the attack, either the 17th or the 18th, while you were still in the village, was the mosque in Sovici being used by the BH army for any military purpose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were asked about the spelling of the name of the man who interrogated you at the school. Do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did he ever write down his name for you so that you knew precisely how it's spelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not. He merely introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, what is his name as you recall it, based on the way he said his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that his name was Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were asked some questions about possible motives --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours. I had to rise to the floor because the transcript again has a completely different surname from the one pronounced by the witness. We all heard it very well and I do not think one even needs the interpretation in your headphones to see the difference in the name that was uttered by the witness and the name that figures in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have come across this issue four or five times, and Mr. Stringer, would you please ask the witness to spell out that name once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please spell the name that we are talking about, as best as you know how to spell it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: I-V-A-N A-N-D-E-B-A-R-K.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were shown a photograph yesterday of a man who interrogated you at the Sovici school. Do you recall that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And the person on that photograph, is that the person whom you are now referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were asked yesterday some questions about possible motives why you surrendered the village at 5.00 in the afternoon on the 17th of April. Why did you surrender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was asked to turn up at Obruc for negotiations, and unless I did so, the whole population of Sovici would be annihilated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At that moment, did the HVO have the capability to annihilate everyone in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In Mostar, when you were working in the area of the Health Centre, you were asked about the incident in which two prisoners were sent to retrieve a body that was in the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who directed the prisoners to go retrieve that body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I learned it afterwards. At that moment, I did not know what the man's name was. But later on, now I know that it was Stela.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At the moment, you didn't know his name. Is that -- did you see that person direct those prisoners to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So is it your testimony you saw a person subsequently known to you as Stela order those prisoners to go retrieve the body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Y [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Thank you for helping us by giving your testimony. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will show you out of the courtroom. We all wish you good luck in the future.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have some exhibits to tender at this time. Exhibit 3.3, which is the map the witness made marks on. Exhibit 6.3 is a photo already in evidence, but we would ask that now the revised version which contain the marks made by the witness be admitted as a new exhibit; the same for the photograph which is 8.2, and also the photograph marked as 6.8. We would also tender the photograph Exhibit Number 39, photographs 20.2 and 20.11, both of which now contain markings made by the witness; and finally, Exhibit 14.5, the photograph of the Health Centre, which now also contains markings made by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about that Exhibit 8.8?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The Exhibit 8.8, Your Honour, is already in evidence because it's among the first admitted. But this is -- the witness didn't make any marks on that photograph, so I think it's unchanged but is already admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We object, Your Honours, only to Exhibit Number 39. Because that photograph was featured more than ten times. It appeared in all the Croatian papers and other papers across former Yugoslavia, and there is a caption clearly indicating who that man is, so the witness could see this picture whenever he liked, and he saw it, just as all of the people who read and followed the press saw it. And as he himself says that he read the press, and it is quite evident that he has been following this trial, that he knows who this man is, and therefore, the identification of that photograph here, we think that it serves no practical purpose in this courtroom, so that we object emphatically to this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. First of all, there's nothing in evidence in this case indicating whether or not that photo was circulated in the media. There's no evidence about that, other than the assertion that has just been made by counsel. That's number one. Number two, counsel had ample time and opportunity to cross-examine the witness on that very point and failed to do so. So for those reasons, we tender the document. The witness recognised the person whose photograph appears in it, and we think it ought to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we believe that -- yes, Mr. Krsnik. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Indeed, there is surprise, and I cannot really believe that my learned friend says what he says. Is he indeed enlightened about this or did somebody misinform him? I do not know. Of course, I will produce evidence to this, but this photograph was made at the funeral of a Croatian soldier, and it was carried by all the Croatian and Bosnian papers. The defence has these newspapers, we have the originals of these newspapers and the Defence, as I say, will have to do it but, evidently, when our turn comes, we shall have to tender it into evidence with a list of all the names. It is not only this individual who attended this funeral; there were other also individuals apart from the photograph used by our learned friends, as you can see from the exhibits. The magazine which first featured that information is called Globus. It has a very large circulation, very popular, much read in Croatia, but it can obtained both in Bosnia, Serbia, and across the former Yugoslavia. So apart from what my learned friend said, there is only my statement to this effect, we shall procure that magazine too and we shall exhibit it to the Court. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no objections to these exhibits, however, I should also like to tender into evidence two photographs and a map that we used. So could the registry please help me with the numbers for the markings.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I believe numbers were given, D2/8 and D2/9.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like to tender them into evidence. And there was a map which was not marked. That was shown the witness. We asked him to draw something on it. He failed to do so, but I would nevertheless like to tender this map into evidence just to show is the map that he was unable to read. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That map will be D2/10.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So we would like to tender that into evidence, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As for the Exhibit P39, which is a photo, this Trial Chamber has made a decision already to admit it into the evidence at the beginning of this trial. So all those documents have been admitted into the evidence. It is the right of Defence counsel to tender your evidence any time you feel it's convenient. It is so decided. So the Madam Registrar will give a proper number for all those documents, I think including that piece of paper with the witness's name on it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Exhibit P3.3, which was the map, is now PP3.3. The annotations made on that map by Witness Y is now PP3.3/1. Exhibit P6.3 is now PP6.3, and the annotations made are -- the Exhibit Number is now PP6.3/1. Also, PP6.8 was already admitted, but annotations were made, so the new exhibit number is PP6.8/1. The same goes for PP20.2; the annotated version is now P20.2/1. Another photo was annotated. That will be PP20.11/1. And one more annotated photo is P14.5/7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about P8.2?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P8.2 also was annotated, and it should be PP8.2/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. So, your next witness, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. The next witness is requesting protective measures. In fact, he is requesting closed session. So I will tender to the Chamber now the written application, which we can discuss. Obviously, we'll want to -- to discuss it, we'll want to be into private session. So if I can have the usher's assistance, I will distribute these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, before you go to the substantial issues, can I ask you to file this motion a little bit earlier so that the registrar or the logistic people could be well prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And you're absolutely right. You'll see that it's dated yesterday. I thought we were going to get -- I thought we had a chance we might get to him yesterday afternoon. And it was prepared and, to be honest, at the end of the day, I forgot about it. If the Chamber does grant the protections, the protections requested are simply -- well, are closed session which, frankly, doesn't require -- it's not like voice distortion, it does not require extensive preparation, but I apologise for not tendering it to you earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There are objections, Your Honour. If I can address it, I'll tell the Chamber the position of the parties. First our position, and I will tell you my consultations with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Slow down, Mr. Scott, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour, I can go through the motion and state the Prosecution's position. I can tell you that I have consulted with Defence counsel, and then perhaps -- obviously you can hear from the Defence. Can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 3.58 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 10th day of October, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
